source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 1 (ISLB A1) · lesson 5. Exercises reused from the lesson.

title.en: Iman: the faith of a Muslim

topic: What faith means, its three parts, and the six pillars

learn.en: Iman is an Arabic word that means faith: trusting Allah with all your heart.
learn.title: What is Iman?

learn.en: Faith is light and doubt is darkness. They are opposites.
learn.title: Light, not darkness

learn.en: True Iman has three parts: the heart believes, the tongue says it, and the body does good actions.
learn.title: Three parts

learn.en: If you love your mum but act unkindly, that isn't real love. Iman is the same: heart, words and actions together.
learn.title: Like real love

learn.en: We believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and destiny — the good and the bad.
learn.title: The six pillars

order.en: Put the six pillars of Iman in order

quiz.en: True or false? Doubt and faith are two opposite things.
True or false? A Muslim believes that only good things come from Allah.
How do we show our true Iman?
opts: Only by thinking about it quietly
With our heart, our tongue and our limbs
Only when we are at school

quiz.en: What does it mean to have faith in someone?
opts: You believe in them with all your heart
You think they might not be telling the truth

think.q: You know telling the truth is right. How can your tongue and your hands show your Iman today?
think.a: Your tongue says kind, honest words, and your hands do helpful things — like picking up a friend's dropped toy.

parents.summary: Iman (faith): believe in the heart, say it with the tongue, show it with actions; and the six pillars of faith.
parents.tip: Count the six pillars of Iman on his fingers together.
